## 7.6 Secondary: Story Engagement → Word Learning (Autistic Females Only)

> **Scope limitation:** The "Autistic Male" sheet of the raw coding file uses a different layout and lacks story engagement columns (visual attention length, story duration). This secondary model is therefore restricted to **female Autistic participants only**. Results should not be generalised to the full Autistic sample. This limitation should be disclosed explicitly in the manuscript.

```{r rq3-story-engagement, results = "markup", echo = TRUE}
# ── Extract story data from raw Excel files ───────────────────────────────────
# ASD: "Autistic Female" sheet of ASD_EngagementCodingRAW_Full.xlsx
#   col 68 = Story Visual Attention Length (sec)
#   col 69 = Story Duration (sec)
#   NOTE: "Autistic Male" sheet uses a different coding format and lacks story columns.
#   Story engagement model is therefore limited to female ASD participants.
#
# NT:  NT_Engagement_SecondaryCoder_raw.xlsx
#   col 59 = Story Visual Attention Length (sec)
#   col 60 = Story Duration (sec)
#
# In both files the story values sit in the participant HEADER ROW
# (the row where col 1 matches "^P\d{3}$").
#
# story_engagement = visual_attention_sec / story_duration_sec  (proportion 0–1)

# ── ASD females ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
asd_xl      <- suppressMessages(
  read_excel(here("R Formatted/ASD_EngagementCodingRAW_Full.xlsx"),
             sheet = "Autistic Female", col_names = FALSE, .name_repair = "minimal")
)
asd_pid_col  <- as.character(asd_xl[[1]])
asd_pid_rows <- which(grepl("^P\\d{3}$", asd_pid_col))

story_asd <- bind_rows(lapply(asd_pid_rows, function(r) {
  data.frame(
    pid = as.integer(sub("^P0*", "", asd_pid_col[r])),
    visual_att_sec = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(as.character(asd_xl[[68]][r]))),
    duration_sec = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(as.character(asd_xl[[69]][r]))),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
})) %>%
  filter(!is.na(visual_att_sec), !is.na(duration_sec), duration_sec > 0) %>%
  mutate(story_engagement = visual_att_sec / duration_sec)
story_asd <- .remap(story_asd)

cat("ASD story data (females only): n =", nrow(story_asd), "participants\n")

# ── NT ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
nt_xl      <- suppressMessages(
  read_excel(here("R Formatted/NT_Engagement_SecondaryCoder_raw.xlsx"),
             col_names = FALSE, .name_repair = "minimal")
)
nt_pid_col  <- as.character(nt_xl[[1]])
nt_pid_rows <- which(grepl("^P\\d{3}$", nt_pid_col))

story_nt <- bind_rows(lapply(nt_pid_rows, function(r) {
  data.frame(
    pid = 2000L + as.integer(sub("^P0*", "", nt_pid_col[r])),
    visual_att_sec = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(as.character(nt_xl[[59]][r]))),
    duration_sec = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(as.character(nt_xl[[60]][r]))),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
})) %>%
  filter(!is.na(visual_att_sec), !is.na(duration_sec), duration_sec > 0) %>%
  mutate(story_engagement = visual_att_sec / duration_sec)
story_nt <- .remap(story_nt)

cat("NT story data: n =", nrow(story_nt), "participants\n")

# ── Descriptives ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
story_all <- bind_rows(
  story_asd %>% mutate(group = "Autistic"),
  story_nt  %>% mutate(group = "Non-autistic")
)

fmt_table(story_all %>%
     group_by(group) %>%
     summarise(
       N = n(),
       `Visual attention (sec): M (SD)` = sprintf("%.1f (%.1f)", mean(visual_att_sec), sd(visual_att_sec)),
       `Story duration (sec): M (SD)` = sprintf("%.1f (%.1f)", mean(duration_sec), sd(duration_sec)),
       `Story engagement (prop): M (SD)` = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f)", mean(story_engagement), sd(story_engagement)),
       .groups = "drop"
     ),
   caption = "Story engagement descriptives (story_engagement = visual attention sec / story duration sec)")

# ── Secondary model: story engagement → word learning (ASD only) ──────────────
asd_story <- base %>%
  filter(group == "Autistic") %>%
  left_join(story_asd %>% select(pid, story_engagement), by = "pid") %>%
  filter(!is.na(story_engagement)) %>%
  mutate(z_story = scale_var(story_engagement))

cat("Story engagement model: N kids =", n_distinct(asd_story$pid),
    "| N trials =", nrow(asd_story), "\n")
cat("Note: ASD story model restricted to female participants (male sheet lacks story columns)\n")

if (n_distinct(asd_story$pid) < 3) {
  cat("NOTE: Too few ASD participants with both story engagement and word learning data to fit model.\n")
} else {
  rq3_story <- glmer(correct ~ z_story + (1|pid),
                     data = asd_story, family = binomial, control = ctrl)

  fmt_table(as.data.frame(round(summary(rq3_story)$coefficients, 3)) %>%
       rownames_to_column("Term") %>%
       rename(b = Estimate, SE = `Std. Error`, z = `z value`, p = `Pr(>|z|)`),
     caption = sprintf("Secondary: Story engagement → word learning, Autistic females only (n = %d children, %d trials)",
                       n_distinct(asd_story$pid), nrow(asd_story)))
}
```

## 7.7 Group × Engagement Interactions

To examine whether engagement channels predict word learning *differently* by group, interaction models were fitted on the combined sample. Two models were run:

- **Model A:** 4 subscales (no Touch; n reported in model output below)
- **Model B:** 5 subscales (with Touch; n reported in model output below)

```{r interaction-models, results = "markup", echo = TRUE}
base_nt_ref2 <- base %>% mutate(group = factor(group, levels = c("Non-autistic","Autistic")))

# Model A: 4 subscales
dA <- base_nt_ref2 %>%
  filter(complete.cases(pick(Proximity,Communication,Eye,Emotion))) %>%
  mutate(across(c(Proximity,Communication,Eye,Emotion), scale_var, .names = "z_{.col}"))
cat("Model A: N kids =", n_distinct(dA$pid), "| N trials =", nrow(dA), "\n")

mA_main <- glmer(correct ~ group + z_Proximity + z_Communication +
                   z_Eye + z_Emotion + (1|pid),
                 data = dA, family = binomial, control = ctrl)

mA_int  <- glmer(correct ~ group*(z_Proximity + z_Communication + z_Eye + z_Emotion) +
                   (1|pid),
                 data = dA, family = binomial, control = ctrl)

anova_A <- as.data.frame(anova(mA_main, mA_int)) %>%
  rownames_to_column("Model") %>%
  mutate(Model = c("Main effects", "Interactions"))
fmt_table(anova_A, caption = "Model comparison: main effects vs interactions, 4-subscale model (Model A)")

# Model B: 5 subscales with Touch
dB <- base_nt_ref2 %>%
  filter(complete.cases(pick(Proximity,Touch,Communication,Eye,Emotion))) %>%
  mutate(across(c(Proximity,Touch,Communication,Eye,Emotion), scale_var, .names = "z_{.col}"))
cat("Model B: N kids =", n_distinct(dB$pid), "| N trials =", nrow(dB), "\n")

mB <- glmer(correct ~ group*(z_Proximity+z_Touch+z_Communication+z_Eye+z_Emotion) +
              (1|pid),
            data = dB, family = binomial, control = ctrl)

fmt_table(as.data.frame(round(summary(mB)$coefficients, 3)) %>%
     rownames_to_column("Term") %>%
     rename(b = Estimate, SE = `Std. Error`, z = `z value`, p = `Pr(>|z|)`),
   caption = sprintf("Model B: Group × engagement interactions on word learning (n = %d children)",
                   n_distinct(dB$pid)))
```

**Result:** Adding interactions did not improve model fit for the 4-subscale model (χ² = 1.70, *p* = .79). In Model B, a significant group × Touch interaction emerged (*b* = –0.72, *SE* = 0.31, *z* = –2.34, *p* = .019). Group-specific simple slopes for Touch (computed via `emmeans::emtrends`, table below) showed Touch was positively associated with word learning in NT children (*b* = 0.47, *SE* = 0.24, *z* = 1.94, *p* = .052) but the slope reversed in ASD children (*b* = –0.25, *SE* = 0.19, *z* = –1.32, *p* = .189). The interaction is significant and indicates reliably different Touch–learning associations between groups, but the ASD slope itself is not significant on its own and should be interpreted with caution given *n* = 55 children (ASD = 20, NT = 35).

```{r modelB-emtrends, echo = TRUE}
if (requireNamespace("emmeans", quietly = TRUE)) {
  emtr <- emmeans::emtrends(mB, ~ group, var = "z_Touch",
                            infer = c(TRUE, TRUE))
  fmt_table(as.data.frame(emtr) %>%
              rename(b = z_Touch.trend,
                     `95% LCL` = asymp.LCL, `95% UCL` = asymp.UCL,
                     z = z.ratio, p = p.value) %>%
              mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 3))),
            caption = "Model B: Group-specific simple slopes for Touch (emtrends)")
}
```

**In plain language:** One unexpected pattern turned up. Among non-autistic children, touching the robot more went along with better word learning. Among autistic children, the trend pointed the other way. The difference between those two patterns is statistically reliable, but the autistic trend on its own is not, and this analysis comes from a smaller subsample (55 children) and was not predicted in advance. Treat it as a lead worth following up, not a finding to build on. One possibility worth testing is that touch means different things in each group, social play for one child and sensory exploration for another.

### Random Slopes Check

```{r random-slopes-check, results = "markup", echo = TRUE}
# Test whether random slopes improve fit (uncorrelated, all 5 measures)
mB_rs <- tryCatch(
  glmer(correct ~ group*(z_Proximity+z_Touch+z_Communication+z_Eye+z_Emotion) +
          (1 + z_Proximity+z_Touch+z_Communication+z_Eye+z_Emotion || pid),
        data = dB, family = binomial, control = ctrl),
  error = function(e) NULL)

if (!is.null(mB_rs)) {
  fmt_table(as.data.frame(anova(mB, mB_rs)) %>% rownames_to_column("Model") %>%
       mutate(Model = c("Random intercepts only", "Random slopes")),
     caption = "Random slopes model comparison")
  fmt_table(as.data.frame(VarCorr(mB_rs)) %>% select(grp, var1, vcov, sdcor) %>%
       rename(Group = grp, Variable = var1, Variance = vcov, SD = sdcor),
     caption = "Random effect variances (random slopes model)")
}
```

**Result:** Random slopes did not improve model fit (χ² = 0.23, *p* = .999) and all slope variances collapsed to zero, indicating that the effect of engagement on word learning does not meaningfully vary across individual children beyond what group membership explains. The random intercept-only structure is retained.

## 7.8 Visualisation — Group × Touch Interaction

```{r plot3-touch-interaction, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5, echo = TRUE}
# Predicted probabilities with 95% CI (delta method)
touch_mean <- mean(dB$Touch, na.rm = TRUE)
touch_sd   <- sd(dB$Touch,   na.rm = TRUE)

grp_levels <- levels(factor(dB$group))

pred_data <- expand.grid(
  z_Touch = seq(-2.5, 2.5, length.out = 100),
  group = factor(grp_levels, levels = grp_levels)
) %>% mutate(
  z_Proximity = 0,
  z_Communication = 0,
  z_Eye = 0,
  z_Emotion = 0,
  pid = NA_real_,
  Touch_raw = z_Touch * touch_sd + touch_mean
)

# Use terms(mB) so the model matrix columns are guaranteed to match fixef(mB)
mm <- model.matrix(delete.response(terms(mB)), data = pred_data)
mm <- mm[, names(fixef(mB)), drop = FALSE]

pred_data$logit <- as.numeric(mm %*% fixef(mB))
pred_data$se    <- sqrt(diag(mm %*% as.matrix(vcov(mB)) %*% t(mm)))
pred_data <- pred_data %>%
  mutate(prob = plogis(logit),
         lower = plogis(logit - 1.96*se),
         upper = plogis(logit + 1.96*se))

ggplot(pred_data, aes(x = Touch_raw, y = prob, colour = group, fill = group)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), alpha = 0.15, colour = NA) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.7) +
  annotate("text", x = 0.6, y = 0.515, label = "Chance", size = 3.5, colour = "grey40") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = pal, name = "Group") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal, name = "Group") +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0,1), labels = percent_format()) +
  labs(title = "Predicted Word Learning by Touch Engagement and Group",
       caption = "Other engagement channels held at mean; word type = POK; shading = 95% CI",
       x = "Touch Score (raw units)", y = "Predicted Probability Correct") +
  theme_pub +
  theme(plot.caption = element_text(size = 9, colour = "grey40"))
```

```{r consort-rq4, echo = TRUE, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4.2}
    "RQ4 Analysis\n",

), title = "RQ4 — Participant Flow: Engagement Group Comparisons")
```

*Do autistic and non-autistic children differ in their engagement with the robot (overall and by channel)?*

## 8.1 Descriptives

```{r rq4-descriptives, echo = TRUE}
means <- .remap(read_csv(here("engagement_overall_means.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)) %>%
  mutate(group = recode(group, "NT" = "Non-autistic", "ASD" = "Autistic"),

desc <- means %>%
  group_by(group) %>%

    .names = "{.col}_{.fn}"))

asd_row <- as.list(desc[desc$group=="Autistic", ])
nt_row  <- as.list(desc[desc$group=="Non-autistic",  ])

desc_long <- bind_rows(lapply(measures, function(m) {
  data.frame(
    Measure = m,
    `ASD M (SD)` = paste0(asd_row[[paste0(m,"_M")]], " (", asd_row[[paste0(m,"_SD")]], ")"),
    `NT M (SD)` = paste0(nt_row[[paste0(m,"_M")]],  " (", nt_row[[paste0(m,"_SD")]],  ")"),
    check.names = FALSE
  )
}))

fmt_table(desc_long, caption = sprintf("Descriptives by group (ASD n = %d, NT n = %d)",
                               asd_row$N, nt_row$N))
```

## 8.2 Mixed Models: Engagement ~ Group

Linear mixed models were fitted for each engagement channel with group (Non-autistic reference) as the fixed effect and random intercepts for child. Models were fitted on the cleaned interval-level data.

> **Sample size note — 4-channel vs Touch model:**
> The four channels Proximity, Communication, Eye Contact, and Emotion are modelled on the **full engagement sample (n = 87; Autistic = 51, Non-autistic = 36)**. This is valid because the data-cleaning pipeline applied a **global session cutpoint** to all 21 children who were asked not to touch: every channel's data was truncated at the interval where the touch instruction occurred, so post-instruction intervals contribute to *no* channel — including Proximity, Communication, Eye, and Emotion. The **Touch model uses the Touch-valid subset only (n = 66)**, as no touch scores exist after truncation. See Section 4.3–4.4 and the touch-cutpoint verification table for confirmation.

```{r rq4-models, results = "markup", echo = TRUE}
d_cleaned <- .remap(read_csv(here("engagement_cleaned_intervals.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)) %>%
  mutate(group = recode(group, "NT" = "Non-autistic", "ASD" = "Autistic"),
         group = factor(group, levels = c("Non-autistic","Autistic")))

rq4_results <- lapply(measures, function(m) {
  dat <- d_cleaned %>% filter(!is.na(.data[[m]]))
  mod <- lmer(reformulate("group + (1|pid)", response = m), data = dat, REML = FALSE)
  cf  <- coef(summary(mod))["groupAutistic",]
  vc  <- as.data.frame(VarCorr(mod))
  icc <- vc$vcov[1] / sum(vc$vcov)

  nt_vals  <- means %>% filter(group=="Non-autistic")  %>% pull(m) %>% na.omit()
  asd_vals <- means %>% filter(group=="Autistic") %>% pull(m) %>% na.omit()
  pool_sd  <- sqrt((var(nt_vals)*(length(nt_vals)-1) + var(asd_vals)*(length(asd_vals)-1)) /
                   (length(nt_vals)+length(asd_vals)-2))
  d_cohen  <- (mean(asd_vals)-mean(nt_vals)) / pool_sd

  data.frame(Measure = m, b = round(cf["Estimate"],3), SE = round(cf["Std. Error"],3),
             t = round(cf["t value"],2), p_raw = as.numeric(cf["Pr(>|t|)"]),
             d = round(d_cohen,2), ICC = round(icc,3))
}) %>% bind_rows() %>%
  mutate(
    sig = ifelse(p_raw < .001, "***", ifelse(p_raw < .01, "**", ifelse(p_raw < .05, "*", "ns"))),
    p   = fmt_p(p_raw)
  )

fmt_table(rq4_results,
   caption = "RQ4: Group differences in engagement (linear mixed models, interval-level data)")

# Random effects variance-covariance for each channel
rq4_vc <- lapply(measures, function(m) {
  dat <- d_cleaned %>% filter(!is.na(.data[[m]]))
  mod <- lmer(reformulate("group + (1|pid)", response = m), data = dat, REML = FALSE)
  vc  <- as.data.frame(VarCorr(mod)) %>%
    select(grp, var1, vcov, sdcor) %>%
    mutate(Measure = m, .before = 1)
}) %>% bind_rows()

fmt_table(rq4_vc %>% rename(Group = grp, Term = var1, Variance = vcov, SD = sdcor),
   caption = "RQ4: Random effects variance components for each engagement LMM (grp = grouping factor, NA in Term = residual)")
```

```{r plot2-engagement, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 5, echo = TRUE}
try(ggplot2::ggsave("figure/fig7_engagement_groups.png", last_plot(), width = 11, height = 5, dpi = 300, bg = "white"), silent = TRUE)
try(ggplot2::ggsave("figure/fig7_engagement_groups.pdf", last_plot(), width = 11, height = 5, bg = "white"), silent = TRUE)
```

**Interpretation:** Autistic children showed significantly lower Communication (*b* = –0.70, *p* < .001, *d* = –0.99) and Eye contact (*b* = –0.84, *p* < .001, *d* = –1.03) than neurotypical children. Proximity, Touch, and Emotion did not significantly differ, though Touch trended (*p* = .074, *d* = –0.45; note reduced ASD *n* due to Touch exclusions).

**In plain language:** The groups engaged with the robot differently in some channels but not others. Autistic children communicated with the robot less and looked at it less, and these were large, reliable differences. But they sat just as close, touched it about as much, and showed similar positive emotion, and the Bayesian checks (Section 9.2) actively supported "no difference" on those three channels. The differences were specific to the classic social-communication behaviours, not a lower level of interest in the robot overall. And as RQ1 to RQ3 show, lower outward engagement did not cost autistic children learning.

# 9. Bayesian Sensitivity Analyses

Bayesian sensitivity analyses were conducted for the three primary null findings using the `BayesFactor` package (Morey & Rouder, 2018). These are **child-level analyses** (one observation per child, using per-child means), and should be interpreted as sensitivity checks rather than direct replications of the mixed models in Sections 5–6, which used interval-level data. The child-level approach is more conservative (smaller effective *N*) and does not account for the nested structure of trials, but provides a useful prior-informed complement to the frequentist results.

**Prior distributions:** Bayesian *t*-tests used a Cauchy prior on standardised effect size (*r* = √2/2 ≈ 0.707; Rouder et al., 2009). This prior places approximately 50% probability on effect sizes smaller than ±0.707 and 50% on larger effects, reflecting agnosticism about direction and magnitude. Bayesian correlation tests used a stretched beta prior on *ρ* with *κ* = 1 (Ly et al., 2016), the `BayesFactor` default, which is uniform on the correlation scale.

**Model comparison:** Each test compares two models — H₀ (null model: no effect) versus H₁ (alternative model: non-zero effect). Bayes Factors quantify the relative predictive adequacy of each model given the observed data.

**BF interpretation framework:** Bayes Factors are reported as BF₀₁ (evidence for H₀ over H₁). Following Jeffreys (1961) as adapted by Lee & Wagenmakers (2013): BF₀₁ > 10 = strong evidence for null; 3–10 = moderate; 1–3 = anecdotal; BF₀₁ = 1 = no evidence either way; BF₀₁ < 1 = evidence favouring H₁. Results in the anecdotal range (1–3) are interpreted cautiously as they are sensitive to prior choice, which is why prior sensitivity analyses are reported.

**Prior sensitivity:** All tests were re-run with *r* = 0.5 (conservative) and *r* = 1.0 (liberal) for *t*-tests, and *κ* = 3 for correlations. Stability of BF₀₁ category across prior specifications is reported in each table.

**Posterior distributions:** The `BayesFactor` package uses a sampling-based approach that does not readily yield full posterior distributions for the parameters of interest. Posterior means and credible intervals are therefore not reported here. Full posterior inference would require a Stan-based implementation, which could not be executed due to a software compatibility issue with the current operating system.

```{r bayes-setup, echo = FALSE}
# Per-child word learning accuracy (≥4/12 threshold already applied upstream)
acc_child <- base %>%
  group_by(pid, group) %>%
  summarise(accuracy = mean(correct, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

# Per-child engagement means (join group from acc_child)
eng <- .remap(read_csv(here("engagement_overall_means.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)) %>%
  select(-any_of("group"))

bay_dat <- acc_child %>%
  left_join(eng, by = "pid")

asd_bay <- bay_dat %>% filter(group=="Autistic")
nt_bay  <- bay_dat %>% filter(group=="Non-autistic")

bf_evidence <- function(bf01) {
  ifelse(bf01 > 10, "Strong null",
  ifelse(bf01 > 3,  "Moderate null",
  ifelse(bf01 > 1,  "Anecdotal null", "Favours H1")))
}

# Helper: Welch t-test + ttestBF at three rscale values
bayes_ttest <- function(x, y, label) {
  x  <- x[!is.na(x) & is.finite(x)]
  y  <- y[!is.na(y) & is.finite(y)]
  tt <- t.test(x, y)
  d  <- (mean(x) - mean(y)) / sqrt((sd(x)^2 + sd(y)^2) / 2)
  bf_default <- 1 / as.vector(ttestBF(x = x, y = y, rscale = sqrt(2)/2))
  bf_cons    <- 1 / as.vector(ttestBF(x = x, y = y, rscale = 0.5))
  bf_lib     <- 1 / as.vector(ttestBF(x = x, y = y, rscale = 1.0))
  data.frame(
    Comparison = label,
    `M ASD` = round(mean(x), 3),
    `M NT` = round(mean(y), 3),
    `n ASD` = length(x),
    `n NT` = length(y),
    t = round(tt$statistic, 3),
    df = round(tt$parameter, 1),
    p = fmt_p(tt$p.value),
    d = round(d, 3),
    `BF01 (r = 0.71)` = round(bf_default, 3),
    `BF01 (r = 0.50)` = round(bf_cons,    3),
    `BF01 (r = 1.00)` = round(bf_lib,     3),
    Evidence = bf_evidence(bf_default),
    check.names = FALSE
  )
}

# Helper: Pearson correlation + correlationBF at two kappa values
bayes_cor <- function(x, y, label) {
  ok <- complete.cases(x, y)
  x  <- x[ok]; y <- y[ok]
  ct <- cor.test(x, y)
  bf_k1 <- 1 / as.vector(correlationBF(x, y, kappa = 1))
  bf_k3 <- 1 / as.vector(correlationBF(x, y, kappa = 3))
  data.frame(
    Channel = label,
    n = length(x),
    r = round(ct$estimate, 3),
    p = fmt_p(ct$p.value),
    `BF01 (k = 1)` = round(bf_k1, 3),
    `BF01 (k = 3)` = round(bf_k3, 3),
    Evidence = bf_evidence(bf_k1),
    check.names = FALSE
  )
}
```

## 9.1 RQ2 — Group Difference in Word Learning

Per-child accuracy compared between ASD and NT using a Welch *t*-test and Bayesian *t*-test.

```{r bayes-rq2, results = "markup", echo = TRUE}
rq2_bay <- bayes_ttest(
  x = asd_bay$accuracy,
  y = nt_bay$accuracy,
  label = "Word learning accuracy (ASD vs NT)"
)
fmt_table(rq2_bay, caption = "RQ2 Bayesian sensitivity: group difference in word learning accuracy (per-child). BF01 reported at three rscale values.")
```

## 9.2 RQ4 — Non-Significant Engagement Channels

Per-child engagement means compared between groups for Proximity, Touch, and Emotion.

```{r bayes-rq4, results = "markup", echo = TRUE}
rq4_bay <- bind_rows(
  bayes_ttest(asd_bay$Proximity, nt_bay$Proximity, "Proximity"),
  bayes_ttest(asd_bay$Touch, nt_bay$Touch, "Touch"),
  bayes_ttest(asd_bay$Emotion, nt_bay$Emotion, "Emotion")
) %>% rename(Channel = Comparison)

fmt_table(rq4_bay, caption = "RQ4 Bayesian sensitivity: group differences in engagement (per-child means). BF01 at three rscale values; Evidence column uses default r=0.71.")
```

## 9.3 RQ3 — Engagement Predicting Word Learning in ASD

Pearson correlations and Bayesian correlation tests between per-child engagement means and word learning accuracy in ASD children.

```{r bayes-rq3, results = "markup", echo = TRUE}
channels_bay <- c("Proximity","Communication","Eye","Emotion","Touch")

rq3_bay <- bind_rows(lapply(channels_bay, function(ch)
  bayes_cor(asd_bay[[ch]], asd_bay$accuracy, ch)
))

fmt_table(rq3_bay, caption = "RQ3 Bayesian sensitivity: engagement ~ word learning correlations in ASD (per-child). BF01 at kappa=1 (default) and kappa=3; Evidence column uses kappa=1.")
```

## 9.4 BF Evidence Plot

```{r bayes-bf-plot, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 5.5, echo = TRUE}
bf_plot_dat <- bind_rows(
  rq2_bay %>% transmute(Label = "Word learning\n(ASD vs NT)", RQ = "RQ2", BF01 = `BF01 (r = 0.71)`),
  rq4_bay %>% transmute(Label = Channel, RQ = "RQ4", BF01 = `BF01 (r = 0.71)`),
  rq3_bay %>% transmute(Label = Channel, RQ = "RQ3", BF01 = `BF01 (k = 1)`)
) %>%
  mutate(
    Label = factor(Label, levels = rev(unique(Label))),
    Evidence = ifelse(BF01 > 10, "Strong null",
               ifelse(BF01 > 3,  "Moderate null",
               ifelse(BF01 > 1,  "Anecdotal null", "Favours H1"))),
    Evidence = factor(Evidence,
                      levels = c("Strong null","Moderate null","Anecdotal null","Favours H1"))
  )

pal_bf <- c("Strong null" = "#2166ac","Moderate null" = "#74add1",
            "Anecdotal null" = "#fdae61","Favours H1" = "#d73027")

ggplot(bf_plot_dat, aes(x = log10(BF01), y = Label, fill = Evidence)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.6) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0,    linetype = "solid",  colour = "grey20", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = log10(3),  linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = log10(10), linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = -log10(3), linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("BF01=%.2f", BF01)),
            x = 0, hjust = -0.1, size = 2.8, colour = "grey20") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal_bf, name = "Evidence") +
  facet_grid(RQ~., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
  labs(title = "Bayesian Sensitivity: Evidence for Null Hypotheses",
       x = "log10(BF01)  [favours H1 <-- 0 --> favours H0]",
       y = NULL,
       caption = "Dashed lines at BF01 = 3 and 10. All analyses at per-child level.") +
  theme_pub +
  theme(strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0, face = "bold"),
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())

# ── save standalone manuscript figure ─────────────────────────────────────────
try(ggplot2::ggsave("figure/supp_s3_bayes_bf.png", last_plot(), width = 9, height = 5.5, dpi = 300, bg = "white"), silent = TRUE)
try(ggplot2::ggsave("figure/supp_s3_bayes_bf.pdf", last_plot(), width = 9, height = 5.5, bg = "white"), silent = TRUE)
```

# 10. Summary of Findings

| RQ | Finding |
|---|---|
| **RQ1** | See result above — GLMM intercept tests overall ASD accuracy vs 50% chance |
| **RQ2** | No significant group difference in word learning accuracy (*p* = .264) |
| **RQ3** | No engagement channel significantly predicted word learning in ASD alone |
| **RQ4** | ASD < NT on Communication and Eye contact (*d* ≈ –1.0, both *p* < .001); other channels ns |
| **Exploratory** | Significant group × Touch interaction (*p* = .019): Touch positively predicts learning in NT, negatively in ASD |

**Measurement note:** Factor analysis revealed fundamentally different engagement structures in ASD vs NT children. No composite engagement scores were created; all five channels were analysed as independent subscales. The "asked not to touch" protocol introduced structured missingness in Touch, particularly in ASD children (20/51 excluded from Touch analysis).
